title: fix: update reports hide missing glibc requirements
body:
Refs #157167. Thanks @PennyVibe for the Ubuntu 20.04 reproduction.

## What Problem This Solves

Update failure reports hide a native addon's missing GLIBC requirement when the loader message follows a worker error or contains private paths.

## User Impact

Reports retain a bounded numeric diagnosis such as `GLIBC_2.33 not found`, while paths, token text, and custom version labels remain redacted. This is diagnostic repair, not a claim that an already-installed 2026.9.5 updater can complete its first upgrade hop. No dependencies, native modes, configuration, or filesystem safety guarantees change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failure-fact owner keeps one diagnostic line, and public reports redact filesystem paths. A loader cause on a later line or after `/lib/...` therefore disappears before report formatting. Extract only the exact numeric missing-GLIBC fact before those existing boundaries, then admit that fixed fact in the public projection.

The ABI and snapshot-copy repairs are already on main: fs-safe 0.20.0 targets glibc 2.28 (#158640), and #154354 uses guarded portable create-only plugin copying instead of a native-only no-replace move. SQLite integrity/content checks remain owned by the snapshot implementation. [fs-safe #709](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/709) separately fixes its move boundary to preserve the original loader cause; it needs a release before consumers can receive that improvement.

The unchanged published 2026.9.5 driver launches its own snapshot worker and fs-safe 0.13.1 before candidate code executes. A newer candidate dependency alone cannot repair that driver. The issue remains open for that first-hop limitation; this PR deliberately uses `Refs`.

## Evidence

- The regression goes through `createUpdateFailureFact` and `prepareUpdateFailureReport`. Both numeric GLIBC cases failed before the production fix; custom/private version labels stayed excluded. The complete report suite passed 103/103 locally. Its wrapper took 55.54 seconds, dominated by shared compiler preparation; the four regression cases took 21 ms in the pre-fix run.
- On Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3g47hmam2dkytra5z1bsb72`, three sequential runs of the report and redaction suites passed, followed by every direct-import sibling found by the required basename search: Doctor maintenance settlement/refusals and trajectory metadata. No barrel re-exports were found.
- The current candidate-state and plugin-tree suites passed with `FS_SAFE_NATIVE_MODE=off`, exercising the existing portable snapshot path. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed, including all selected typechecks, lint and guards. The final combined command exited 0 in 23m52.871s; source-file SHA-256 checks matched the reviewed local patch. [Testbox environment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36282621846).
- Ubuntu 20.04/glibc 2.31: published GNU fs-safe 0.18.1 fails to load with GLIBC_2.33 (its symbols also require 2.34); published GNU 0.20.0 loads, preserves collisions, and completes an uncontested no-replace move. Its ABI gate reports maximum GLIBC_2.28. The musl package fails to load on this glibc host. [Addon proof environment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36282682763).
- The untouched published 2026.9.5 snapshot entry point reproduced the original failure against the published 2026.9.6 target on Ubuntu 20.04/Node 26.5.0 in 564 ms. All five synthetic source files stayed byte-identical, SQLite integrity was `ok`, and scratch was removed. This is a failing real snapshot-boundary cell, not successful full-update/current-candidate proof. [Published driver environment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36283372204).
- Fresh isolated Codex review through P1: scoped-clean. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Production +11/-2 LOC; tests +51/-0; docs +12/-0. PR CI timing is not yet available; auto-merge is off.

Draft promotion gate: REST confirmed `mergeable: true`, but the GitHub CLI write guard rejected `draft=false` as an unsupported pull-edit field. The lane requires REST publication, so this PR remains draft; no guard bypass or auto-merge was used.
